result:
Three non-attacking rooks must occupy three distinct rows and three distinct columns. Since the rooks are indistinguishable, a placement is determined by:

1. Choosing which 3 of the 6 rows are used: $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ ways.
2. Choosing which 3 of the 6 columns are used: $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ ways.
3. Matching the chosen rows to the chosen columns one-to-one: $3! = 6$ ways.

Each choice of rows, columns, and matching gives a distinct set of rook positions, and every valid placement arises exactly once this way. So the count is

$$\binom{6}{3}^2 \cdot 3! = 20 \cdot 20 \cdot 6 = 2400.$$

ANSWER: 2400
